clue.text: A student of life fluttering by

definitions.text: A student of life fluttering by

parts.words: A student of life fluttering by
parts.note: the life that flutters by is butterflies and moths, so this is a scientist who studies them

explanation.surface: A naturalist idly watching the world flit past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Life fluttering by' sounds like time passing, but it means insects on the wing: the student is a collector of butterflies and moths.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the specialist who studies butterflies and moths, the order of winged insects.

clue.text: Grandee angered

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Grandee angered (7)': the anagram of GRANDEE has no indicator, so 'angered' would have to be both the anagram signal and the definition.

clue.text: First person with goods vehicle for John in Moscow

parts.note: the first person singular pronoun is I
a van carries goods

explanation.surface: A delivery driver with a van being given a Russian name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'John in Moscow' asks for the Russian form of the name John.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan is the Russian equivalent of the English given name John.

clue.text: He has a row with little Arabs in sultanate

indicators.note: the little Arabs are placed inside the word for the sultanate

parts.note: Oman is a sultanate on the Arabian peninsula
Ar is an abbreviation of Arab or Arabic, so little Arabs are ARS

explanation.surface: A man quarrelling with some young Arabs in a Gulf state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' reads as a quarrel but means rowing a boat; 'little Arabs' are the abbreviations AR, made plural.
explanation.definitionFit: A rower pulls oars, so he is the one who has a row on the water.

clue.text: One is neither here nor there in it

definitions.text: One is neither here nor there in it

parts.words: One is neither here nor there in it
parts.note: describes the state of being on the way between two places, having left one and not reached the other

explanation.surface: Someone feeling indecisive and out of place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neither here nor there' usually means irrelevant; here it is taken literally, someone between departure and arrival.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on the move between places, not yet at a destination, is being on the way.

clue.text: Letters are carried in this stick at Brighton

definitions.text: Letters are carried in this stick at Brighton

parts.words: Letters are carried in this stick at Brighton
parts.note: the seaside sweet sold at Brighton has the resort's name running through it

explanation.surface: A postbag carried on a walking stick by the seaside.
explanation.walkthrough: Brighton is an English seaside resort; its striped stick of hard candy has the town's name in letters running all the way through. 'Letters' suggests post.
explanation.definitionFit: Seaside candy sticks with lettering through them are a traditional English souvenir sold under this name.

clue.text: Dusty establishment where cuts produce much whining

definitions.text: Dusty establishment where cuts produce much whining

parts.words: Dusty establishment where cuts produce much whining
parts.note: the cuts are made by blades in timber, and the whining is the screech of the machinery, with sawdust everywhere

explanation.surface: A grubby workplace where budget cuts cause endless complaining.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cuts' and 'whining' suggest spending cuts and grumbling staff; they are saw cuts and the noise of the blades.
explanation.definitionFit: A timber yard where logs are sawn into planks is noisy and full of sawdust.

clue.text: Temporarily leading the team as Hook in Peter Pan, for example

definitions.meaning: a stand-in skipper holds the post for the time being

definitions.text: as Hook in Peter Pan, for example
definitions.meaning: the actor playing the pirate Captain Hook in the play is performing the role of a captain

explanation.surface: A stand-in skipper compared with a pantomime villain.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the phrase: the actor is acting the part of a captain.
explanation.definitionFit: A deputy given a skipper's rank for the time being; also a performer playing the pirate captain on stage.

clue.text: Unrestrained D.I.Y. hordes beat bus-stops here

indicators.note: hordes let loose run wild, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the initials of do-it-yourself, taken as letters
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Gangs of home-improvement enthusiasts running riot at bus stops.
explanation.walkthrough: DIY plus HORDES plus BEAT gives thirteen letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Bus stops stand at the edge of the street, alongside the kerb.

clue.text: A privateer of crude-sounding demeanour

indicators.note: the word for crude is said out loud to give the first part

parts.note: crude means coarse
an air is a manner or demeanour

explanation.surface: A pirate with rough manners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coarse' said out loud gives CORS; add AIR.
explanation.definitionFit: A privateer was a licensed pirate, especially one sailing from the Barbary coast.

clue.text: Cunning route out of the cloister

definitions.note: describes a passage under a curved span leading from the cloister

parts.note: arch means sly or cunning
a way is a route

explanation.surface: A crafty monk's escape path from the monastery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cunning route out' suggests a sly escape; the definition is the vaulted passage leading out of the cloister.
explanation.definitionFit: A vaulted passage is the usual exit from a monastery's covered walk.

clue.text: He incited black jealousy dramatically, giving one a turn

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
a go is a turn in a game

explanation.surface: A stage villain stirring up envy and giving someone a fright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Black jealousy' points to Othello, the Moor of Shakespeare's play, whose jealousy the villain stirs.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's villain in Othello goads the Moor into murderous jealousy.

clue.text: Either a ruin or a success with hit

definitions.meaning: a wreck or crash that ruins things
a big hit show or record

explanation.surface: Something that is either a disaster or a triumph after a blow.
explanation.walkthrough: The word serves as a crash, a box-office triumph and a verb for striking hard.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a crash or wreck, a runaway success, and to strike violently.

clue.text: Sling one's hook if turned to silence?

indicators.note: the little word if is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: sh is a call for silence

explanation.surface: Being told to get lost after being hushed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sling one's hook' is British slang for clear off, but here it means casting a fishing hook.
explanation.definitionFit: Casting a baited hook is the act of angling.

clue.text: Darling little girl to stop in Wyoming

indicators.note: the word for stop goes inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: WY is the postal abbreviation for Wyoming
end means stop

explanation.surface: A sweet little girl coming to a halt in a western state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Darling' is an endearment in the surface but a surname here: the Darling family's daughter in Peter Pan.
explanation.definitionFit: In Peter Pan, the eldest Darling child is the girl who flies to Neverland.

clue.text: Surprised when taken against the mast

definitions.meaning: a sail blown back against the mast by a head wind

explanation.surface: A sailor caught off guard when the wind shifts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken aback' means startled; a sail is aback when the wind presses it flat against the mast.
explanation.definitionFit: Startled, as in the idiom about being caught off guard; and in sailing, sails pressed backward by a head wind.

clue.text: Unruly gun dog seizing Eric's first 14

indicators.note: the rearranged dog letters grab and hold the next letter inside them
an unruly animal is out of control, so these letters run riot into a new order
only the opening letter of the name is used

explanation.surface: A badly behaved retriever grabbing hold of a man called Eric.
explanation.walkthrough: '14' is a cross-reference: the answer to 14 across, so the definition is another word for that, a freshwater species.
explanation.definitionFit: The gudgeon is a small freshwater species of the carp family.

clue.text: In piping form

parts.note: shaped like a pipe, hollow and cylindrical, while also suggesting being in fine voice

explanation.surface: A singer in fine voice.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaped like a tube or pipe; hollow and cylindrical.

clue.text: Shorten a river crossing?

parts.note: a bridge carries a road across a river

explanation.surface: Asking whether a river crossing could be made shorter.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut down a text is to condense it.

clue.text: Roll of workers includes a baker

indicators.note: the list of workers takes in the letter A within it

parts.note: a roster is a list of who works when

explanation.surface: A staff list that names a baker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Baker' looks like a person on the roll, but means something that bakes: an oven or a roasting tin.
explanation.definitionFit: An oven or roasting dish bakes meat, so it is a cooking appliance.

clue.text: Wandering sailor turning up in shower of rice

indicators.note: the turned sailor sits inside the scattered rice
a shower scatters rice, so its letters are thrown into a new order
in a down clue the word for sailor is turned upward, read backwards

parts.note: tar is a term for a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor turning up at a wedding amid thrown rice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shower of' looks like a description of confetti at a wedding but signals a rearrangement; 'turning up' suits a down clue, where the sailor reads upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Something irregular and unpredictable in its course strays or roams.

clue.text: Dashed if such a bloomer should be protected from the blast

definitions.text: bloomer should be protected from the blast
definitions.note: a flowering shrub that is tender and needs shelter from cold winds

indicators.note: dashed means smashed or knocked about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An exasperated gardener on a tender shrub that needs shelter from wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dashed' reads as a mild oath but rearranges IF SUCH A.
explanation.definitionFit: This flowering shrub with drooping blooms is frost-tender in many gardens, so needs shelter.

clue.text: To Wilde it meant the unspeakable in pursuit of the uneatable

definitions.text: To Wilde it meant the unspeakable in pursuit of the uneatable

parts.words: To Wilde it meant the unspeakable in pursuit of the uneatable
parts.note: Oscar Wilde's quip described English country gentlemen on horseback chasing a fox

explanation.surface: Oscar Wilde's famous jibe at country sport.
explanation.walkthrough: The line is from Wilde's play A Woman of No Importance, describing the English gentleman galloping after a fox.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilde's famous line mocks riders with hounds chasing a fox.

clue.text: Sin to note consuming strong drink — and done in the bath?

indicators.note: the sin and note together swallow the drink inside them

parts.note: taken as written
G is a musical note
gin is a strong spirit

explanation.surface: A sinner drinking gin while relaxing in the tub.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as an example: the tub is only one place people croon.
explanation.definitionFit: Crooning or vocalising is a classic activity in the tub.

clue.text: Kate reformed at 7,probably

definitions.note: points to 7 down, a timber-cutting yard, where a hardwood would likely be found

indicators.note: the name is formed again in a different order

explanation.surface: A woman called Kate turning over a new leaf at seven o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: '7' looks like a time, but refers to the answer at 7 down, the timber yard, where this hardwood is cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard tropical timber is the sort of wood cut into planks at a timber yard.

clue.text: Substitute for characters 24 and 25

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for
the 24th and 25th letters of the alphabet are X and Y

explanation.surface: A stand-in for the answers at 24 and 25 across.
explanation.walkthrough: '24 and 25' look like cross-references to this puzzle's clues, but count letters of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand-in authorised to act, or vote, on behalf of another person.

clue.text: The burden lifted from tobacco's non-users

indicators.note: the letters are taken straight out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Non-smokers relieved of a weight.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs inside 'non-users'.
explanation.definitionFit: A responsibility or obligation that weighs on someone is a load to bear.

clue.text: Stud manager

definitions.meaning: a raised knob or stud, as on a shield
the person in charge at work

explanation.surface: The man who runs a stud farm.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised ornamental knob; and the person in charge, the chief.

clue.text: When marriage decree is in reverse

indicators.note: the two little words are written backwards

explanation.surface: Asking when a divorce ruling comes into force.
explanation.walkthrough: The Latin word means 'unless'; a decree of this kind ends a marriage only after a waiting period, so the definition names the provisional divorce decree.
explanation.definitionFit: The provisional English divorce order is called a decree by this Latin name, meaning 'unless'.

clue.text: Awkward riot after inter national anthem

indicators.note: the rearranged letters come behind the abbreviation

parts.note: INT is a short form of international

indicators.note: awkward means clumsy and disordered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fans rioting after an international match during the national anthem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Anthem' suggests a national song, but it is the hymn sung at the start of Mass.
explanation.definitionFit: The opening chant or psalm sung as the priest approaches the altar is a church anthem.

clue.text: Unidentified ten initially dine out as one

indicators.note: the letters named are taken out of the long word, the rest staying in order
only the first letter of ten is used

explanation.surface: An unknown group of ten going out to dinner together.
explanation.walkthrough: From UNIDENTIFIED take out T (ten initially) and the letters of DINE; what remains is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Joined together so as to act together, made into a single whole.

clue.text: Collected snippets of paper

parts.note: articles clipped from newspapers and kept, the paper being a newspaper

explanation.surface: A scrapbook of paper scraps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paper' suggests scrap paper; it means newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Articles clipped from newspapers and gathered together are clippings.
